question: What is the primary focus of indirect nursing care technologies?

options.A: Managing resources and data behind the scenes
options.B: Administering intravenous medications at the bedside
options.C: Conducting direct surgical procedures in theatre

explanation: Indirect care technologies support the clinical environment and workflow without requiring direct physical contact with the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why are indirect care technologies important in a busy hospital setting?

options.A: They ensure patients never experience any clinical complications
options.B: They minimize administrative burdens and reduce human error
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for clinical documentation
options.D: They replace the need for professional nurses on the ward

explanation: Automating behind-the-scenes tasks frees up time and decreases mistakes related to manual record-keeping. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do RFID systems track hospital equipment and patients?

options.A: Using high-resolution security camera facial recognition
options.B: Using electromagnetic fields to read attached tags
options.C: Relying on constant physical headcounts by ward clerks
options.D: Requiring manual barcode scans for every single item

explanation: RFID technology utilizes radio waves to automatically track tags placed on assets or people. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: A nurse needs to locate a missing infusion pump quickly on a busy ward. Which technology provides real-time tracking of this mobile equipment?
explanation: RFID tracking displays the real-time location of movable medical assets on a dashboard, saving search time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is a major function of an electronic inventory system in a hospital?

options.A: Evaluating the bedside clinical competence of interns
options.B: Monitoring stock levels and tracking expiration dates
options.C: Tracking the physical location of wandering patients
options.D: Scheduling nurse shift rotations for the monthly roster

explanation: Electronic inventory platforms keep track of medical supplies, usage rates, and expiry dates to prevent shortages. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: An automated supply system alerts ward management when gauze stocks are low. What clinical problem does this prevent?

options.A: Unexpected stockouts during emergency wound dressings
options.B: Overstaffing of nurses on the morning shift
options.C: Delays in physician medical diagnosis writing
options.D: Inaccurate vital sign documentation in patient charts

explanation: Automated reorder triggers ensure that necessary clinical consumables do not run out unexpectedly. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: What data do computerized staffing systems use to predict nursing workload?

options.A: Historical patient admission trends and acuity
options.B: The personal home addresses of the nursing staff
options.C: Physical maintenance logs of hospital elevators
options.D: The daily cafeteria menu selections of patients

explanation: Staffing algorithms analyze past admission patterns and patient illness severity to forecast staffing needs. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why is scheduling staff based on patient acuity better than simple headcounts?

options.A: It matches staff numbers to the actual clinical workload of the patients
options.B: It ensures all patients are discharged within twenty-four hours
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for night shift allowances
options.D: It guarantees that every nurse gets every weekend off duty

explanation: Acuity-based staffing ensures sicker patients who require more care have enough nurses assigned to them. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: What does system integration achieve in a hospital software environment?

options.A: Connects different software modules into a unified platform
options.B: Separates the pharmacy database from the nursing ward
options.C: Replaces all computer hardware with paper records
options.D: Increases the amount of redundant manual data entry

explanation: Integration links separate systems so data flows smoothly between departments without repetitive entry. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: A hospital uses fragmented, unlinked systems for records and supplies. What is the most likely consequence for the nursing staff?

options.A: Experiencing immediate elimination of all administrative tasks
options.B: Spending extra time entering the same data multiple times
options.C: Enjoying flawless coordination across all hospital units
options.D: Having instant access to real-time automated stock alerts

explanation: Unintegrated systems force workers to duplicate data entry, increasing frustration and administrative workload. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge for health technology adoption in low-resource settings?

options.A: Resistance to digital change among traditional workers
options.B: An immediate surplus of highly trained software engineers
options.C: High financial costs for equipment maintenance and repairs
options.D: Erratic and unreliable public electrical power supply

explanation: A surplus of engineers is not a challenge; rather, technical skill shortages and infrastructure deficits are major hurdles. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is it important to teach nursing informatics early in nursing training programs?

options.A: To eliminate the need for pharmacology and anatomy classes
options.B: To prepare graduates for increasingly digitalized healthcare workplaces
options.C: To ensure students never have to perform bedside patient care
options.D: To replace traditional clinical nursing skills with computer programming

explanation: Early informatics education equips future nurses with the digital literacy needed for modern hospital environments. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h6)
